In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data do not support a picture of multiple scattering in the sense of the Glauber theory, but that the data are compatible with a picture where the proton interacts with one nucleon only.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a single nucleon is a good probe to study the structure of the nucleus.
the multiple scattering analysis of the inclusive cross sections at 100 Gev/c is a useful method for studying the structure of the proton.
the multiple scattering is the main source of the nuclear effects in the pA collisions at 100-GeV/c.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the multiple scattering effects are very strong and must be taken into account in the analysis of hadron–nucleus collisions.
the inclusive cross section is dominated by a contribution from a proton-nucleon collision.
